WHY THERE IS NO xor_reference. The field's own contract is that the reference IS the claim. rc1 could name one because a second, independently synthesised, placed, CTS'd and routed stream existed that was INTENDED to be identical, so a zero XOR was a reproducibility result. rc2 has no such sibling: it is a single-lineage ECO chain, and every stream on disk that could be offered as a reference is one this candidate is MEANT to differ from -- rc1's shipped bytes (292 cells and their routing), rc2's own pre-logo signoff stream (the logo), rc2's control arm (the VIA3.R.4 edit). Naming any of them would render a red row for an intended difference, and a gate that is red by construction is the one its reader learns to skip. The row is left NOT-MEASURED with the gate's own reason rather than answered with a reference chosen to have a row.

NARROW THE ENTRY, DO NOT DELETE IT -- and the argument for narrowing rather than deleting is the whole content of this decision.
  THE CASE FOR DELETING IT: rc1's own withdraw_when named a condition, that condition has been met by measurement rather than by argument, the numbers are from this build's own signoff run at the stated derate over an unchanged analysis population, and leaving an entry standing after its stated condition is met is how a known_bad list rots into noise nobody reads.
  THE CASE FOR KEEPING IT, WHICH WINS: rc1's entry explicitly forked. Branch one -- 'if the ruling is the flat guess, the endpoints must be FIXED' -- is now satisfied. Deleting the row now would record that the derate question was closed, when what actually happened is that the design moved to the safe side of an unanswered question. That is precisely the substitution -- a measurement standing in for a decision -- this list exists to prevent.
  SO: the FEP half is withdrawn and stated as withdrawn; the derate half stands, narrowed to exactly what it now is -- a signoff margin whose size is a guess, with the design now on the conservative side of it and with no characterised data to say by how much. known_bad.what: CARRIED UNCHANGED FROM rc1 AND STILL LIVE. Every published stream in this project carries an Artifactory property named `layout.canonical_hash`, written by scripts/ci/gds_canonical_hash.py. The name reads like a layout identity and the value cannot support that reading: measured 2026-08-26, KLayout strmxor 0.30.10 reported NO DIFFERENCES between two streams across all 49 layer/datatype pairs while their canonical hashes DIFFERED at identical byte count (302,688,050) and identical record count (34,791,830), because write_stream is not order-deterministic. rc2 gives that its own corroboration without an XOR: outputs/nanosoc_eth_chiplet_pads_rc2.gds (md5 0b72b1301f2087f943bb0c3dabcb2731) and outputs/nanosoc_eth_chiplet_pads_rc2v3r4ctl.gds (md5 9769ede7851d5bd466c1f06102e8306d) are two write_stream invocations of the same unedited geometry, identical in size at 309,421,274 bytes and different in md5.
known_bad.decision: NOT withdrawn and NOT rewritten. The digest is correct for what it computes and the raw md5/sha256 beside it are load-bearing -- a foundry Final Report cites the md5. What is wrong is the DIRECTION a reader may take from it, so gds_canonical_hash.py now returns a `claim` field saying a MATCH implies the same layout and a MISMATCH implies nothing, and the layout question is answered separately by scripts/ci/gds_xor_arbiter.py. NOTE FOR THIS CANDIDATE: that arbiter has no reference to run against here (see `supersedes`), so on rc2 the canonical hash is the ONLY digest-shaped thing in the record and the temptation to read it as a layout answer is correspondingly larger.
known_bad.withdraw_when: the store stops publishing this digest under a `layout.*` name -- either renamed to something that says RECORD SEQUENCE, or accompanied by the gds-layout-identity gate's verdict as a sibling property. Until then, treat a `layout.canonical_hash` mismatch as a prompt to run the arbiter and never as a finding.
